rules.rationale: Chalcogenide anions raised refractive index in dielectric source; polarizability raises phonon DOS peaks.
Post-transition main-group heavy elements raised source objective; high Z raises phonon frequencies.
Moderate concentration balances polarizability and bonding complexity.
Mid mean Z covers chalcogenides and post-transition heavy elements.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers chalcogenide and heavy-element polarity effects from dielectric refractive index; fails if phonon peaks are dominated by light-element modes.

rules.rationale: Halides lowered source objective; weak halogen bonds give low phonon energies.
Quinary and senary compositions are rare and poorly sampled; their negative source effect is unreliable.
Light nonmetals lowered source objective; low Z lowers phonon frequencies.
Low mean Z covers light nonmetals and rare quinary-senary compositions.

skills.hypothesis: Reverses the low-confidence halogen and quinary-seinery source relations; fails if halides and rare quinary-senary compositions actually carry high-lying peaks.

lesson: Across eight development seeds, both skills showed similar mean AUCs (61.4 vs 62.6 then 47.2 vs 46.0) and final best scores (72.3 vs 79.8 then 75.2 vs 64.5). The polarity transfer skill reached the maximum score twice while the counter-hypothesis reached it once, suggesting the chalcogenide polarity mechanism remains the better-grounded transfer direction.
revision_summary: Retained the chalcogenide and heavy-element polarity transfer skill and replaced the light-element counter-hypothesis with a reversal of the low-confidence halogen and quinary-seinery source relations. Kept the same two-to-four mechanistically interpretable rules per skill, and did not use placeholder keys or target outcomes. Selected the polarity transfer skill for deployment.
